I'm an M.S. student in economics at Texas A&M University, graduating in May 2027.
My research interests are behavioral and experimental economics, industrial
organization and market design.

I’m interested in what people do with the information they have, and what happens
when getting a better answer takes work. I came to that question through Federal
Reserve forward guidance: what can a market price tell someone who already has
public information and needs to make a decision?

My working paper takes that question to weather, where I can compare market
prices with public forecasts and see what happened the next day. I also work on
an empirical industrial organization replication and am developing a question
about how rewards and disclosure shape firms’ willingness to experiment. I
share the papers and the questions behind them on the
[Research & Projects](research.qmd) page. I’d be glad to hear what those questions
bring to mind, including papers or settings I should look at.

I'm looking for predoctoral research positions starting in summer 2027.
